title: Clicking Name flips the Categories list between Z to A and A to Z every time
custom_preconds:
Setup (manual QA tester and Claude session)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in as an Admin at {Location-A} (for example Staging Heavy Duty - 9919), with the Settings - Parts permission.
  • Category {Category-A} (for example ZZAUTOTEST-PC27 alpha) exists.
  • Category {Category-B} (for example ZZAUTOTEST-PC27 Beta) exists.
  • Category {Category-C} (for example ZZAUTOTEST-PC27 tier 10) exists.
  • No other category name starts with the same tag (for example ZZAUTOTEST-PC27).
  • You are on a page other than Categories, so the list opens sorted by Name A to Z.
custom_steps:
1. Go to Settings and click Categories in the Parts group of the Settings menu.
  2. Move the mouse pointer away from the column headers.
  3. Read the order of {Category-A}, {Category-B} and {Category-C}.
  4. Click the Name column header.
  5. Move the mouse pointer away from the column headers.
  6. Read the Name header arrow and the order of {Category-A}, {Category-B} and {Category-C}.
  7. Click the Name column header again.
  8. Move the mouse pointer away from the column headers.
  9. Read the Name header arrow and the order of {Category-A}, {Category-B} and {Category-C}.
  10. Click the Name column header a third time.
  11. Move the mouse pointer away from the column headers.
  12. Read the Name header arrow and the order of {Category-A}, {Category-B} and {Category-C}.
  13. Click the Name column header a fourth time.
  14. Move the mouse pointer away from the column headers.
  15. Read the Name header arrow and the order of {Category-A}, {Category-B} and {Category-C}.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 3: the rows read {Category-A}, {Category-B}, {Category-C} (alpha, Beta, tier 10) and the Name header arrow points up.
  • Step 6: the list is now Z to A. The Name header arrow points down and the rows read {Category-C}, {Category-B}, {Category-A} (tier 10, Beta, alpha).
  • Step 9: the list is back to A to Z. The Name header arrow points up and the rows read {Category-A}, {Category-B}, {Category-C}.
  • Step 12: the third click flips the list again, to Z to A, the same order as after the first click in step 4. The Name header arrow points down and the rows read {Category-C}, {Category-B}, {Category-A}. The list does not go back to an unsorted or opening order.
  • Step 15: the fourth click flips it again, to A to Z. The Name header arrow points up and the rows read {Category-A}, {Category-B}, {Category-C}.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-11258; story SV-10134 (Story 1, Categories, sort by name; story text re-synced to the PRD on 13 Oct 2026); PRD "Settings Pricing And Categories Sorting (Price/Category)", Confluence 578781186, version 21 (14 Oct 2026), S1-R5, S1-R6, S1-R6a, S1-R7, §2 Sort arrows, §4 Key Decisions 'A header toggles; there is no third state', read 14 Oct 2026; design canvas board 1.2 (Categories - after), 13 Oct copy, unchanged on 14 Oct. Source-verified 14 October 2026; not yet build-verified (no Price/Category QA build exists).

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S1-R5: “When the user clicks the Name header while the sort is ascending, the list re-sorts into descending order, Z to A.”
  • S1-R6: “When the user clicks the Name header while the sort is descending, the list re-sorts into ascending order, A to Z.”
  • S1-R6a: “Every further click on the Name header flips the direction again. There is no third state.”
  • S1-R7: “The Name column header arrow always shows the direction that is currently applied.”
  • PRD §2 Sort arrows: “Each click on the header being sorted flips its direction. A third click gives the same order as the first click. No click clears the sort or returns the list to its opening order.”
  • PRD §4 Key Decisions: “A header toggles; there is no third state. The first click sorts the column, the second reverses it, and the third gives the first click's order again.”
